messages:
customer-bob: Hey team, since ~08:12 UTC we're seeing a mix of 429s + 5s tail latencies for requests from EU users. Some requests get routed to US and show auth failures after retrying. Impacting checkout flow.
support_jen: sorry to hear that, can you paste a couple of curl logs and the org/app id?
customer-bob: app=acme-checkout org=acme-co. Example: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_...\" -d '{\"input\":\"x\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` returns 429 from `eu-west-1` then client retries and hits `us-west-2` and gets `401` with same token (weird). Logs: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 8
X-Region: eu-west-1
--- retry ---
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
X-Region: us-west-2```
support_jen: thanks. tagging infra/eng. @eng-runtime-sam can you check routing/fallback behavior and whether retries can land in different region with stale auth state?
eng-runtime-sam: looking. quick note: routing uses regional affinity + fallback. If eu capacity exhausted we fanout per policy and may route to next available region. Usually auth is checked at the control plane, but there are edge caches that can cause transient 401 if token revocation propagated slowly.
eng-runtime-sam: can you run a repro for me? steps I'd try: 1) set `X-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1` 2) hammer 200 concurrent short requests (eg `hey -n 5000 -c 200 -H \"X-Prefer-Region: eu-west-1\" ...`) 3) watch headers `X-Region`, `X-Fallback-Route`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-Req-Id`.
customer-bob: can run now, starting a short run. will paste sample headers.
customer-bob: sample sequence from reproduction: ```Req 1: X-Region: eu-west-1 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 HTTP/1.1 429
Req 2 (client retry after backoff): X-Region: us-west-2 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 45 HTTP/1.1 401```
infra-ryan: quick context: we have per-region token auth caches that obey a 30s TTL for revocation state. If a token was rotated/invalidated in EU but control-plane sync hasn't reached US cache yet, a retry to US could succeed or fail depending on timing. But 401 on US after 429 from EU sounds like an auth edge getting a different state — we should verify whether the client retried with the same Authorization header or mutated it.
ops-ana: also worth noting: burst credits for eu-west are depleted for this org (saw a spike) so fallback policy kicked in. When fallback occurs, there is an internal header `X-Fallback-Reason: capacity` and we set `X-Fallback-Path: eu->us`. That should preserve idempotency keys but if clients retry without `Idempotency-Key` some server-side billing attribution can appear doubled.
support_jen: customer, did you see Idempotency-Key on your retries?
customer-bob: no, our client retrier is naive. we just do exponential backoff but no idempotency header.
eng-runtime-sam: that explains billing weirdness. Recommended short fixes: - add `Idempotency-Key` per logical request - honor `Retry-After` header and apply jitter/backoff - prefer region header to reduce fanout. Longer-term: we'll look at strengthening auth cache invalidation and adding a region-consistent auth check before billing is recorded.
infra-ryan: can you grab traces for a couple of the Request IDs? use `rictl traces fetch --req 0x9ab3 --since 30m` (internal). If you paste two Req-Ids I'll pull end-to-end logs and show where fallback happened.
customer-bob: two ids: 0x9ab3 and 0x9ab7.
eng-runtime-sam: got them. quick findings: 0x9ab3: EU ingress returned 429 after queue threshold hit, control plane created a fallback route to US, request retried by client and hit US edge which checked token state and returned 401 (token flagged as rotated 10s earlier). There's no double-charging in the code path we use for 429+retry if idempotency set; without it the downstream billing event was recorded when the request entered US runtime.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy `runtime-edge:v3.9.2` started 1713601000 by deploy-pipeline, affected ~12% of eu-west-1 shards.
ops-ana: that can make behavior noisier — different edge versions have slightly different auth cache timings. Sam, can we identify which shard served the failing requests?
eng-runtime-sam: yes, the traces tie the failing requests to shard eu-3 (canary fraction). We'll open a short rollback/roll-forward action.
support_jen: escalating to SRE now and creating a support ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INC-2024-328 (customer impact: checkout 15% failure for EU users).
infra-ryan: mitigation checklist for now: 1) advise customer to add `Idempotency-Key` and `X-Prefer-Region` 2) increase client retry backoff to honor `Retry-After` 3) we can temporarily bump reserved capacity for acme-co in eu-west (ops), or route their traffic to dedicated pool if they want zero-fanout.
support_jen: customer-bob, will coordinate ops on capacity bump and keep you posted in this thread. thanks for the repro — very helpful. :thumbsup:
